Is TK41 the same strain as Gushers?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Triangle Kush × Gelato #41
Breeder: Connected Cannabis Co.
THC Content: 20–28%
CBD Content: Low to trace, generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Tropical fruit, sweet berries, creamy vanilla
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

TK41 belongs to the group of modern cannabis strains that became famous under more than one name. Often encountered as White Gushers or simply Gushers, the strain combines Triangle Kush with Gelato #41, bringing Florida-style OG fuel together with the creamy dessert genetics that helped define California marijuana during the Gelato era.

Connected Cannabis Co., one of the brands most closely associated with the cultivar, officially identifies the pairing as Triangle Kush × Gelato #41 and describes the finished flower as an indica-dominant hybrid with prominent limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool. The sensory experience is equally divided between its parents. Sweet tropical fruit and cream sit over gasoline, earthy Kush, subtle coffee, and spice, while a powerful cerebral onset gradually expands into a calmer physical state. Dense flowers, substantial trichome coverage, and THC levels commonly landing well above 20% have helped TK41 become far more than another temporary dessert-strain release.
Genetics and Lineage

The documented TK41 lineage is Triangle Kush × Gelato #41. Connected Cannabis Co. describes the cultivar as combining a legendary OG Kush line with its Gelato #41 selection, specifically noting how Triangle Kush pushes diesel and rocket-fuel characteristics into the finished flower while Gelato adds a smoother, coffee-like quality. The genetics are commonly associated with the Cookies Fam breeding circle and Connected Cannabis Co., two closely linked names in the development and distribution of California’s Gelato-era cultivars.

Triangle Kush supplies the older half of the pedigree. Originating from Florida’s influential Kush scene, the cultivar is prized for earthy gas, strong potency, stretching growth, and the deeply recognizable OG character found throughout countless American hybrids. Gelato #41 comes from a completely different direction. A selected Gelato phenotype descended from Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint GSC , it contributes creamy sweetness, colorful flowers, resin production, and a more polished dessert quality. Bringing those parents together gave breeders a way to preserve serious Kush fuel while adding the visual appeal and sweetness that dominated premium cannabis markets during the late 2010s.

TK41 is also closely associated with the White Gushers and Gushers names. Verified nursery material identifies White Gushers as the original Triangle Kush × Gelato #41 Cookies-family cut and describes TK41 as another name for that selected phenotype. This naming overlap can create confusion, particularly because unrelated hybrids sometimes appear under similar Gushers branding. When identifying authentic TK41 genetics, Triangle Kush × Gelato #41 is the defining parentage.
Effects and Experience

TK41 can begin with considerably more mental intensity than its indica-dominant classification suggests. Connected characterizes the high as strong, edgy, and alert, which fits the Triangle Kush side of the cross particularly well. Shortly after consumption, thoughts may feel more animated and sensory details more pronounced. Music, food, conversation, gaming, or creative activities can become unusually engaging, while an elevated mood often accompanies the cerebral shift. Experienced consumers may find the opening functional enough for relaxed social settings rather than immediately feeling confined to the couch.

Time changes the balance. The initial mental edge gradually becomes smoother as physical relaxation develops through the shoulders, limbs, and lower body. Moderate consumption may leave enough clarity for entertainment or casual activities while reducing the desire to rush from one task to another. Larger amounts are more likely to reveal the Kush-heavy side of the genetics, producing slower movement, heavier eyelids, and a preference for remaining comfortable in one place.

Potency varies considerably between crops. Commercial TK41 flower commonly appears around the low-to-mid 20% THC range, while carefully cultivated expressions can climb toward the upper 20s or beyond. That strength means inexperienced marijuana consumers should approach the strain conservatively. Excessive THC may produce dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, temporary memory disruption, racing thoughts, or anxiety before the heavier relaxation becomes apparent.
Medical Benefits

The two-stage effect pattern can make TK41 interesting to medical marijuana consumers who want both a mental shift and later physical relaxation. Some patients gravitate toward this type of cannabis when temporary stress, reduced appetite, tension, low mood, or physical discomfort makes it difficult to settle down. The relatively lively beginning can be preferable to cultivars that immediately produce substantial fatigue, while the later body component may become more useful as the day winds down.

Terpene composition offers additional information about how individual batches may differ. Connected Cannabis Co. identifies D-limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool as prominent components of its Gushers/TK41 products. Limonene generally contributes bright citrus aromatics, caryophyllene adds peppery spice and woody depth, and linalool can introduce softer floral notes. Other cultivated expressions may contain more myrcene, reinforcing earthy and herbal characteristics.

Those compounds are useful for describing the flower, but they do not establish TK41 as a proven treatment for anxiety, depression, chronic pain, insomnia, or another medical condition. The cultivar itself has not undergone clinical trials demonstrating strain-specific therapeutic effectiveness. Patients should examine the laboratory report for the actual product being purchased and consult an appropriate healthcare professional when prescription drugs or significant health conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

TK41’s aroma shows the parents pulling in opposite directions. Gelato #41 contributes sweet cream, fruit, berries, and occasionally vanilla-like softness, while Triangle Kush pushes sharp fuel and earthy OG directly through the sweetness. Connected emphasizes diesel gas and rocket fuel along with a coffee-like tone from Gelato #41. Other well-preserved expressions can reveal tropical fruit, tart candy, grape, or berry before the heavier Kush notes become obvious.

The inhale often begins smoother than the aroma suggests. Cream and sweet fruit arrive first, followed by a citrus edge that can become more noticeable in limonene-rich batches. Midway through the palate, the strain becomes considerably less dessert-like. Fuel, roasted coffee, soil, pepper, and pine begin replacing the initial sweetness, leaving a lingering OG-style finish after exhalation.

That contrast is what keeps TK41 from tasting like another interchangeable Gelato descendant. The cannabis retains enough sweetness to satisfy consumers drawn to modern California flavor profiles, yet the Triangle Kush ancestry keeps gasoline, earth, and spice firmly in the foreground. A careful cure enhances that separation, whereas poorly stored weed may lose its brighter fruit and cream notes and taste disproportionately earthy.
Growing Information

TK41 is a photoperiod cultivar generally requiring approximately eight to ten weeks of indoor flowering. Verified White Gushers/TK41 nursery material places the flowering period within that range and describes the plant as having roughly 1.7-to-2-times stretch after the transition into bloom. That means indoor growers should control height before flowering rather than assuming its indica-dominant classification will result in a compact plant.

Topping, low-stress training, and Screen of Green cultivation can help distribute branches horizontally and create a more evenly illuminated canopy. Triangle Kush can contribute significant stretch, while Gelato #41 adds dense, resinous flower development. Removing weak lower branches before the later flowering stages redirects energy toward stronger tops and improves circulation through the interior of the plant. Support may become necessary as mature flowers accumulate weight.

Humidity control deserves particular attention. Dense, heavily frosted marijuana flowers can retain moisture when foliage is crowded or air movement is inadequate. Consistent circulation, sensible late-flowering humidity, and sufficient spacing between branches reduce the chance of mold developing inside mature colas. Growers should avoid aggressive training late in bloom because damaged branches have little time to recover before harvest.

Outdoor plants perform best where autumn weather remains relatively dry. An early-to-mid-October harvest is a practical expectation for many Northern Hemisphere gardens, although phenotype and latitude can shift maturity. Resin color and flower development should ultimately determine the cutting date. After harvest, slow drying at controlled temperature and humidity helps preserve the tropical fruit, cream, coffee, and fuel aromatics that make TK41 distinctive.
FAQ
What are the genetics of TK41?
TK41 is Triangle Kush × Gelato #41. Connected Cannabis Co. officially identifies this parentage for its Gushers products, which are closely associated with the TK41 and White Gushers names.
Is TK41 the same strain as Gushers?

TK41 is widely used as another name for the Triangle Kush × Gelato #41 cultivar commonly sold as Gushers or White Gushers. Verified Cookies-family clone material specifically identifies White Gushers and TK41 as the same genetic selection. Names can vary between markets, so checking the listed genetics remains the best way to confirm identity.
Is TK41 indica or sativa?

TK41 is generally considered an indica-dominant hybrid, often described around 60% indica and 40% sativa. Connected Cannabis Co. officially categorizes its Triangle Kush × Gelato #41 flower as an indica-dominant hybrid.
How strong is TK41?

Most flower falls somewhere around 20–28% THC, although potency changes with phenotype and cultivation. Its strength, coupled with a fast cerebral onset, makes cautious dosing advisable for consumers without substantial THC tolerance.
What does TK41 taste like?

The flavor combines tropical fruit, sweet berries, cream, and subtle vanilla with diesel fuel, coffee, earth, citrus, and pepper. Connected specifically highlights Triangle Kush’s diesel and rocket-fuel influence alongside Gelato #41’s smoother coffee-like qualities.
Final Thoughts on TK41

TK41 works because neither half of its pedigree completely overwhelms the other. Triangle Kush contributes the deep fuel, earthy structure, and unmistakable OG personality that helped shape American marijuana breeding, while Gelato #41 brings creamier sweetness, resin, color, and contemporary bag appeal. The result became known under several names—TK41, Gushers, and White Gushers—but the Triangle Kush × Gelato #41 genetic foundation remains the constant.

Its effects are just as balanced in progression. A strong, alert cerebral beginning gradually gives way to a calmer and more physically relaxed experience, creating more dimension than a cultivar designed purely for sedation. Add dense trichome-coated flowers and an aroma that moves between tropical candy and rocket fuel, and it becomes easy to understand why this cannabis has remained relevant long after many Gelato-era hybrids disappeared. For consumers who want modern sweetness without sacrificing classic Kush gas, TK41 remains one of the more recognizable bridges between those two generations of weed.
